title: [finding] content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx states `unique` as `boolean`, default `false` — wrong scope vocabulary, and wrong default for autonumber after #13894
body:
Found while implementing #13894 (autonumber fields default to `unique: 'organization'`). Hand-written page, so it does not regenerate itself; filed rather than edited in the #13894 PR per the dispatch's scope fence (that card lands in `packages/spec`).

**Where:** `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`, the common-properties table row:

```
| `unique` | `boolean` | `false` | Enforce uniqueness |
```

**What is wrong (two things, one pre-existing):**

1. **Type.** The contract has been `boolean | 'global' | 'organization'` since ADR-0120 D1 (the scope vocabulary), and the same page already uses `unique: 'organization'` in its own example (`{ name: 'email', ..., unique: 'organization' }` near the top). The row still says `boolean`. Pre-existing.
2. **Default.** After #13894 the default is type-conditional: `false` on every type except `autonumber`, where an omitted `unique` resolves to `'organization'` (one holder per organization, the tenant-composite index). The row's unconditional `false` is now wrong for the one type where the default matters most.

**Suggested fix:** one row edit — type `boolean \| 'global' \| 'organization'`, default `false` (`'organization'` on `autonumber`), description pointing at the generated reference (`/docs/references/data/field`, which carries the full rule from the `.describe()`), plus a sentence in the autonumber section of the same page saying the number is unique per organization by default and that `unique: false` is the explicit opt-out for a display-only sequence.

Refs: #13894 (parent), ADR-0120.

Blocked-by: #13894
